chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalhub, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

The child of fornication and the son of li'an inherit from their mother and their maternal uncles, or their maternal agnates.' The explanation in this narration is that it is permissible that the narrator heard this ruling regarding the son of li'an and assumed that the ruling of the child of fornication is the same, so he narrated it based on his assumption without direct hearing, with the understanding that this is a singular report (shadh) and it is not abandoned because of it the hadiths that we have previously presented.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a child of fornication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, Ali ibn Abi Talib establishes that the child of fornication and the son of li'an inherit from their mother and maternal kin, distinguishing them from the general rule of excluding them from paternal inheritance. Al-Tusi contextualizes this as a singular report (khabar shadh) where the narrator likely conflated the rulings, yet he affirms its validity without overturning the established consensus on the matter.
